task: Determine the evidential stance of the complete window toward the specified cybersecurity aspect. Threat stance is not emotion.

labels.SUPPORTING: The observed evidence materially supports that the target aspect is present in this window.
labels.CONTRADICTING: The observed evidence materially supports a benign or alternative interpretation that conflicts with the target aspect. Mere absence of attack evidence is not contradiction.
labels.NEUTRAL: The evidence is unrelated, non-decisive, or compatible with both the target aspect and an alternative interpretation.

insufficient_context: Mark true when the available window does not permit a defensible stance. This flag is separate from the three semantic labels.
decisive_evidence_ids: List only evidence identifiers that directly justify the selected stance, separated by semicolons. Do not create new identifiers.
rules: Judge only the supplied evidence and aspect definition.
Do not infer an attack solely from unusual volume or timing.
Do not label a benign-only window as CONTRADICTING solely because the target aspect is absent.
Use NEUTRAL when evidence concerns a different attack aspect.
Set insufficient_context=true when a reliable decision requires evidence outside the supplied window.
Confidence must be an integer from 1 (very uncertain) to 5 (very certain).

reconnaissance.definition: Evidence indicating discovery, probing, enumeration, or information gathering that can prepare a later intrusion.
reconnaissance.include: Scanning, service discovery, host discovery, systematic probing, or repeated exploratory communication.
reconnaissance.exclude: Routine isolated service contact without an exploratory pattern.

initial_access_foothold.definition: Evidence indicating an attempt to obtain or maintain an initial presence in the target environment.
initial_access_foothold.include: Exploit-like access behavior, suspicious authentication or login activity, and communication consistent with foothold creation.
initial_access_foothold.exclude: Ordinary authorized access or unrelated discovery behavior.

lateral_movement.definition: Evidence indicating movement, access, or propagation from one internal system or trust boundary to another.
lateral_movement.include: Abnormal internal-to-internal access, remote-service use, or multi-endpoint propagation consistent with campaign progression.
lateral_movement.exclude: Expected internal service communication without movement evidence.

data_exfiltration.definition: Evidence indicating unauthorized transfer, staging, or removal of data from the monitored environment.
data_exfiltration.include: Outbound transfer behavior, unusual volume or asymmetry, or a campaign-consistent channel for removing data.
data_exfiltration.exclude: Routine outbound communication without evidence of data removal.
